verdicts.title: Binding sliding-window parity covers only mistral and ministral; the four other windowed families are untested
verdicts.reasoning: Verified every link. packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:57 still reads _SLIDING_WINDOW_FAMILIES = {"ministral", "mistral"}, and test_sliding_window_parity (:305-340) is the only binding-window model-level parity case, parametrized over exactly those two. I enumerated the default config of all 26 supported_families() on the installed transformers 5.15.1 and reproduced the claim's list: cohere2 4096, deepseek_v4 128, exaone4 4096, gemma2 4096, gemma3 (Gemma3TextConfig) 4096, gpt_oss 128, mellum 1024, ministral 4096, mistral 4096, olmo3 4096. I then ran the exact hypothetical test (assert_parity_forward with sliding_window=4, seq_len=16, both use_attention_mask values, plus the non-binding sliding_window=64 vacuity guard) for gemma2, gemma3, cohere2, exaone4, olmo3, phi3 and mellum: all of them except mellum produce a genuinely binding window (logits differ from the open-window control), so five to six further families could be covered by the existing harness with no new machinery. mellum's window is vacuous (layer_types are all full_attention), and gpt_oss/deepseek_v4 are already excluded by _STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES (I confirmed gpt_oss fails parity for unrelated shim reasons), so the honest count of missing testable families is five, not six. The gap currently hides exactly one live mismatch: gemma2 with attn_logit_softcapping=None and attention_mask=None fails the hypothetical test with abs_err=5.30e-01, which is the softcap=None fallthrough at packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/attention.py:729-738, where vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2 delegates to vmap_sdpa_attention_forward without forwarding sliding_window. Two secondary details in the finding are overstated: gemma2's binding window is not entirely untested (packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/components/test_attention.py:316 exercises vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2 with sliding_window=3 against a dense reference, but only with softcap=1.0), and the fix sketch's request to 'assert parity with attention_mask=None' is already satisfied by the existing use_attention_mask parametrization. Severity stays low: this is a test-coverage finding, the one defect it masks needs a non-default gemma2 config (shipped Gemma2 checkpoints set attn_logit_softcapping=50.0) plus attention_mask=None, and no tracked issue covers it (#813 is about converting parity skips to xfail and the gpt2 gradient mismatch; #963 is a perf item).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: The model-level binding-window parity test is parametrized over {ministral, mistral} only, so a sliding-window regression in the five other families whose default config carries a real window (gemma2, gemma3 text, cohere2, exaone4, olmo3) ships green. Establishing this concretely: running the existing assert_parity_forward harness with sliding_window=4/seq_len=16 (plus the sliding_window=64 vacuity control) over those families shows the window binds for all of them and parity holds today in 9 of the 10 (family x attention_mask) cases -- the single failure is gemma2 with the non-default attn_logit_softcapping=None and attention_mask=None, abs_err=5.30e-01, caused by attention.py:729 dropping sliding_window when softcap is None. So the gap is a real, cheaply closable coverage hole that today masks one non-default-config forward mismatch; it does not by itself cause a wrong result at defaults.

verdicts.title: The #895 dataset guard covers the scoring half only: train_subset()/train_indices() still accept a dataset the partition was not built from
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced exactly on the current tree. packages/opaque-auditing/src/opaque/api/auditing/_coin_flip.py:189 is verbatim 'size = self.dataset_size if dataset_size is None else dataset_size' with no consistency check when both are known, and :209 is 'return Subset(dataset, self.train_indices(len(dataset)))', so train_subset always supplies an explicit size and the recorded dataset_size is never consulted on that path. The symmetric guard added by the #895 fix exists only on the scoring side (attacks/_helpers.py:152-178: the length comparison raising 'scoring requires the full concatenated dataset' plus the index-bounds check). My repro matched the finding's output character for character: coin_flip(ConcatDataset([base32, canaries8]), num_canaries=8, candidate_indices=range(32,40), key=key(0)) records dataset_size=40 with out_indices=[34 35 33 32 36]; cf.train_subset(base32) returns 32 rows, excludes nothing, and raises nothing, while cf.train_subset(audited) correctly returns 35. The milder variant also holds: a CoinFlip built on a 20-row dataset with out_indices=[8 6 15] accepts a different 30-row dataset (train_subset -> 27 rows) and even train_indices(999) -> 996 indices. No existing test pins the override as intentional: test_audit.py:325 and :563 call train_indices with an explicit size on CoinFlips built directly by the _flip helper (no recorded dataset_size), and test_audit.py:342 only asserts train_indices() == train_indices(len(dataset)) for the consistent case, so raising on a contradiction would not break the suite. Severity lowered/held at low: this is a fail-open on caller misuse in the auditing tooling, not a defect in any privacy mechanism, it needs the user to hand a different dataset object to train_subset than the one coin_flip was built on, and the consequence is an audit that under-reports rather than a live epsilon understatement. Not covered by any open tracked issue (#376 is null calibration, #828 is the v_k bound).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: CoinFlip.train_subset(dataset) calls train_indices(len(dataset)), and train_indices prefers an explicit size over the recorded one, so neither method ever compares the caller's dataset against CoinFlip.dataset_size -- the check the #895 fix added on the scoring side only. Reproduced: a CoinFlip built on the 40-row concatenated dataset (dataset_size=40, out_indices=[34 35 33 32 36]) accepts cf.train_subset(base_32rows) and silently returns all 32 base rows with no canary excluded, and a CoinFlip built on 20 rows accepts a different 30-row dataset (27 rows returned, excluding rows 8/6/15 of the wrong object). A user who makes that dataset mix-up trains a target with no held-out canary; the later scoring call against the correct concatenated dataset passes the length check, and the audit reports an uninformative estimate instead of raising. Requires caller misuse; no effect on any accounted epsilon.

verdicts.title: #895 compares dataset length only, so an equal-length reordering is still scored silently
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced. The only identity evidence _scoring_loader compares is len(dataset) against coin_flip.dataset_size plus an index-bounds check (packages/opaque-auditing/src/opaque/api/auditing/attacks/_helpers.py:152-178), and _IndexedCanaries.__getitem__ (:88-89) indexes whatever object it is handed with the partition's canary indices. No fingerprint field exists on CoinFlip (_coin_flip.py:163-168 lists only num_canaries, canary_indices, _in_mask, in_indices, out_indices, dataset_size). My repro on a 20-row TensorDataset with 5 canaries: correct scoring gives [-4, -49, -25, -81, -169] for canary ids [1 6 4 8 12] and one_run -> auc=1.0; scoring the same rows under a random permutation (Subset(ds, perm)) returns [-400, -16, -196, -121, -64] with no error at all, and one_run accepts it (auc=0.3333). So the fail-open entrance is real. Two caveats that cap the severity. First, OPQ-352's own fix sketch called the content fingerprint 'optional', so the missing half was explicitly discretionary rather than an omission from a required fix. Second, the claim's realism argument does not hold: the shuffling the repo's documented pipelines perform is DataLoader(shuffle=True) over the training subset (docs/tutorials/privacy_auditing.ipynb:271), which never touches the object passed to the scorer; no doc or example re-orders the scoring dataset, so hitting this needs the caller to pass a reordered same-length view. Severity low: caller misuse, auditing tooling only, no effect on any accounted epsilon, and the audit direction is under-detection. Not covered by an open tracked issue.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: The #895 scoring guard compares only len(dataset) (attacks/_helpers.py:152-162) while _IndexedCanaries (:88-89) indexes the caller's object by the partition's canary indices, so a same-length reordering passes both new checks. Reproduced on a 20-row TensorDataset with 5 canaries: correct scores [-4, -49, -25, -81, -169] (one_run auc=1.0) versus scores from a randomly permuted Subset of the same rows [-400, -16, -196, -121, -64] (one_run auc=0.3333), with no exception raised on the permuted path. The scores then belong to different records than the coin flips label and the audit silently measures nothing. Reaching this requires the caller to hand the scorer a reordered view of the audited dataset; the shuffling the repo's own tutorials perform is on the training DataLoader, not the scoring dataset, so the documented flows are unaffected.

verdicts.title: The grid-floor justification comment cites a measurement that does not reproduce, and the test validates the floor only at n=1
verdicts.reasoning: All three sub-claims independently reproduced. The comment is at packages/opaque-auditing/src/opaque/api/auditing/one_run/_estimate.py:34-42 above _MIN_GRID_SIZE = 1_000 (:44) and asserts 'at grid_size=16 a fully separable 500/500 canary split audits as eps=0'. I built a 500/500 fully separable estimate (best r=1000, u=0) and measured GdpMethod(grid_size=g).epsilon_at(delta=1e-5): grid 16 -> 32.801667, 64 -> 37.275869, 1_000 -> 38.246718, 10_000 -> 38.246718 -- matching the finding's numbers exactly and contradicting the comment. I also swept separable splits at m=50/100/500/1000/2000 and delta in {1e-5, 1e-3}: grid 16 returns 11.5 to 36.8, never 0, so there is no reading of 'fully separable' under which the comment's measurement holds. The configuration that does collapse is u=250 (75 % attack accuracy): grid 16 -> 0.0, 64 -> 2.700027, 1_000 -> 5.075480, 10_000 -> 5.108089 -- which is precisely the case the #829 regression test builds and describes ('500/500 split whose best threshold makes exactly 250 errors', packages/opaque-auditing/tests/auditing/test_gdp.py:288-320). The comment's second claim is also accurate as reported: TestVKGridConvergence (test_gdp.py:144-158) parametrizes only _compute_v_k(1, 1, ...) against Phi(-mu/2), i.e. the n=1 Bayes error, which constrains nothing about the high ranks that dominate the Chernoff sum for a 10^3-10^4-canary audit. Finally the finding's own concession checks out: grid 1_000 tracks grid 10_000 to 0.033 absolute at u=250, so the constant itself is fine and only the recorded justification is wrong. Severity low and category comment-accuracy are right: no runtime behavior is affected, the public factory still enforces the floor (test_grid_size_below_floor_raises), and the stated harm is a future maintainer misreading the rationale. I did not treat #845 ('Sweep C -- verify every citation against its record') as a duplicate: that is a broad citation-audit sweep, not this specific mismeasured justification.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: The comment justifying _MIN_GRID_SIZE = 1_000 (one_run/_estimate.py:34-42) records a measurement that does not reproduce: a fully separable 500/500 split (r=1000, u=0) audits as eps=32.80 at grid_size=16, not eps=0 (37.28 at 64, 38.25 at 1_000 and 10_000), and no separable split at m=50..2000 or delta in {1e-5, 1e-3} returns 0 at grid 16. The configuration that actually collapses is u=250 -- eps 0.0 at grid 16 versus 2.70 at 64, 5.08 at 1_000, 5.11 at 10_000 -- which is the case the #829 regression test itself constructs and documents. The comment's companion claim that the floor 'is validated against the v_k order-statistic identity' overstates the landed test, which checks only v_1 = Phi(-mu/2) at n=1 and would pass at grid 16 too. Runtime behavior is unaffected and the constant is adequate (grid 1_000 tracks 10_000 within 0.033 at u=250); the defect is a wrong recorded rationale plus a test that cannot fail for the reason the floor exists.
